newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa Q2 net profit boosted by one-off items.
newsitem.headline: Televisa Q2 net profit boosted by one-off items.

text.p: One-off items sharply boosted Mexican television company Televisa's towering second quarter 4.895 billion peso net profit, the company said Thursday.

"Excluding non-recurring items net of realized tax benefits, net income in the second quarter of 1997 would have been 136.82 million pesos compared to a net loss of 51.40 million in the same period of 1996," Televisa said.
Its second quarter net profit including non-recurring items followed a net loss of 279.68 million pesos in the same period a year ago.
Most of this year's net profit was an extraordinary item related to the restructuring of Televisa's stake in PanAmSat, the company said.
Operating income for the second quarter was 342.66 million pesos, compared to 84.33 million pesos in the year-ago period.
In addition, it noted that its second quarter television sales -- 59.3 percent of the company's total sales -- jumped by 24.6 percent to 1.962 billion pesos compared to the year-ago quarter.

The figure was boosted by campaign spending in Mexico's freest elections ever on July 6, as well as aggressive advertising by financial institutions to win workers over to newly private pension funds.

In addition to the seasonal surge in advertising, Televisa said export programming sales, promotional services and revenue from magazine advertising helped lift net sales to 3.309 billion pesos in the second quarter, a 17.6 percent rise from 2.814 billion pesos in the second quarter of 1996.
"The increase in net sales reflected increases in net sales in all of the company's business segments," Televisa said.
In publishing net sales, the increase was 7.4 percent to 599.82 million pesos.

Televisa said its cost of sales rose 15.2 percent to 1.991 billion pesos in the second quarter compared to the year-ago period. It cited costs of special events and sports promotions, the operation of a new U.S.-Mexico border station and the distribution of magazines in the international market for the higher costs.
The integral cost of financing loss fell by 41.79 million pesos in the second quarter of 1997 to 31.40 million pesos from 73.19 million pesos in the year-ago period.
The company said it held 74.2 percent of the viewing audience share from sign-on to sign-off in June, up from 72.9 percent in May and down from 74.7 percent in April.
